title: Porridge
subtitle: Creamy oat porridge with honey and toasted almonds
excerpt: Porridge made with rolled oats and whole milk is one of the most sustaining breakfasts there is. Cook it slowly and stir often for a creamy, thick result. Honey and toasted almonds finish it off well.
sourceNotes: Porridge has been a staple breakfast in Scotland and northern England for centuries. Oats cooked in milk became widespread in Britain through the 19th and 20th centuries.

content.text: Use rolled oats rather than instant oats. They take a few minutes longer but give a creamier texture with more body. Stir almost constantly once the milk heats up to prevent sticking.
If using flaked almonds: toast them in a dry pan over a medium heat for 2 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Put the oats and milk in the saucepan over a medium heat.
Stir continuously as the milk heats up. This stops a skin from forming.
Once the mixture begins to bubble, reduce the heat to low.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Add a small pinch of salt and stir through.
Spoon into bowls. Top with honey and toasted almonds if using.

items.symptom: The porridge has caught on the bottom of the pan.
items.cause: Heat was too high or stirring was not frequent enough.
items.fix: Stir from the bottom and add a splash more milk to loosen.

items.cause: It cooked too long or the ratio was slightly off.
items.fix: Stir in a splash of hot milk until the right consistency.

items.symptom: The porridge is too thin and watery.
items.cause: Too much milk or insufficient cooking time.
items.fix: Keep cooking on low heat and stir until thickened.
